summary_html: Child safely **reunified with parent or guardian**, case closed. Federal policy treats reunification as the preferred outcome once risk factors are mitigated. In Alabama the age of majority is 19 (Ala. Code § 26-1-1), and for child abuse and neglect reporting a "child" is a person under 18, or a person under 19 who is in need of protective services and does not qualify for adult protective services (Ala. Code § 26-14-1(3)).
authority_html:
- **Adoption and Safe Families Act (ASFA)** — establishes reunification timelines and permanency goals  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funds reunification services and tracks permanency outcomes

key_cases.case_name: H.H. v. Baldwin County Department of Human Resources
key_cases.court: Court of Civil Appeals of Alabama
key_cases.holding: The court held that reasonable reunification efforts are excused when a parent has abandoned the child, but that a termination judgment cannot rest on that exception without an express juvenile-court finding of abandonment, and remanded for a specific finding as to whether and when abandonment occurred.
key_cases.relevance: Reunification remains the statutory goal unless an aggravated circumstance such as abandonment is expressly found.
key_cases.quote: we agree with the general proposition that reasonable efforts to reunite a parent with a child are not required when a parent has abandoned the child

key_cases.case_name: P.S. v. Jefferson County Department of Human Resources
key_cases.court: Court of Civil Appeals of Alabama
key_cases.holding: The court reversed a termination judgment because DHR never identified the mother's parenting defect, never communicated what she needed to change, and was relieved of reasonable efforts when the child was five months old, so no clear and convincing evidence satisfied Ala. Code 12-15-319(a).
key_cases.relevance: Reunification cannot be declared impossible when the parent was never told what to fix.
key_cases.quote: DHR did not provide the mother the opportunity to correct any conduct or condition that might have been a barrier to reunification with the child

key_cases.case_name: Montgomery County Department of Human Resources v. A.S.N.
key_cases.court: Court of Civil Appeals of Alabama
key_cases.holding: The court reversed judgments declining to terminate parental rights, holding that the father had abandoned the children so no reasonable efforts were owed him, and that DHR had made reasonable efforts as to the mother, who failed to avail herself of the services offered.
key_cases.relevance: Reunification efforts end where the parent abandons the child or refuses to use the services provided.
key_cases.quote: DHR has no duty to make reasonable efforts to rehabilitate a parent who has abandoned his or her child

key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court reversed a termination judgment because the record did not clearly and convincingly show that the trial court had examined all viable alternatives, including relative placement and continued visitation, and remanded for that consideration.
key_cases.relevance: The Court faulted DHR for having made no recent reunification effort and no current assessment of the mother, treating continued reunification work as part of the alternatives inquiry.
key_cases.quote: the trial court also must find by clear and convincing evidence that there are no viable alternatives to the termination of parental rights

key_cases.case_name: V.M. v. State Dept. of Human Resources
key_cases.court: Court of Civil Appeals of Alabama
key_cases.holding: The court reversed judgments terminating a mother's parental rights as premature, holding that she had accomplished all but one DHR goal and had been sober for nearly a year so that her ongoing rehabilitation was itself a viable alternative, that the maternal grandmother had never been evaluated as a relative resource, and that DHR carries an affirmative duty to facilitate reunification under the federal consent judgment.
key_cases.relevance: A parent who is visibly working the plan cannot be written off; reunification remained the required goal while the mother was still completing her last goal.
key_cases.quote: Pursuant to the terms of a consent judgment in federal litigation, DHR has an affirmative duty to facilitate family reunification whenever that goal is possible.

state_agency.name: Alabama Department of Human Resources
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call your county DHR office, listed at dhr.alabama.gov/county-office-contact, or local law enforcement

extended_foster_care_age: Up to age 21 (Ala. DHR Child and Family Services Plan 2025-2029: youth 17 and older plan "steps to leave foster care at age 21"; a youth who leaves the department's custody after 18 is eligible to return to care before 21)

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met
